hero.title: Token development: build, distribute and launch responsibly
hero.subtitle: Write an ERC-20 from scratch, assemble real tokens with audited libraries, add permit, voting and vesting, learn NFTs and vaults, and design tokenomics that are fair and honest. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can design, build and plan the launch of a token, or explain honestly why a project does not need one.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Complete the token design and the final assessment.

faq.q: Does the platform run my Solidity?
faq.a: No. The labs check your designs, analysis and calculations. You run the code in your own tools on a test network.

faq.q: Is this legal or investment advice?
faq.a: No. It is education. Rules about tokens vary by country, so take advice from a qualified lawyer before issuing or selling any token.

faq.q: Should every project have a token?
faq.a: No. The course teaches you to ask whether a token is needed at all, and it is fine to conclude that a simpler tool is better.

activities.title: Decimals: what the contract really stores
activities.objective: Convert between human-friendly token amounts and the whole numbers stored in the contract.
activities.scenario: Tokens store whole numbers only. A token with 6 decimals stores 1.0 as 1,000,000. Work out the stored values for a payment.
steps: In B7 work out the number of base units in one token: 10 to the power of the decimals (B2).
In B8 work out the stored amount for the human amount in B3.
In B9 convert it back to tokens by dividing B8 by B7.
In B10 work out the smallest possible unit as a fraction of one token.
In B11 work out the stored amount of a 12.75 fee (B4).

checks.label: B7 is the base units per token
checks.hint: =POWER(10,B2)
checks.explain: Ten to the power of the decimals.

checks.label: B8 is the stored amount
B9 is back in tokens
B10 is the smallest unit
checks.hint: Try the formula =1/B7 here.

checks.label: B11 is the stored fee

activities.title: Calculate a vesting schedule
activities.objective: Work out how many tokens are released at a given month under a cliff and linear vesting.
activities.scenario: A team member is granted 1,200,000 tokens, vesting linearly over 48 months with a 12-month cliff. How much is released after 24 months?
steps: In B7 work out the tokens released at month B5: zero before the cliff, otherwise the grant times months elapsed divided by the total months, never more than the grant.
In B8 work out the tokens still locked.
In B9 work out the amount released each month after the cliff.
In B10 work out the months remaining.
In B11 work out the percentage released.

checks.label: B7 is the released amount
checks.explain: Zero before the cliff, otherwise a linear share capped at the grant.

checks.label: B8 is the locked amount
B9 is the monthly amount
B10 is the months remaining
B11 is the percentage

activities.title: How vault shares grow in value
activities.objective: Work out share prices and the shares minted for a new deposit in a yield vault.
activities.scenario: A vault holds 100,000 assets against 100,000 shares. It earns 5,000 in yield. A new user deposits 21,000.
steps: In B7 work out the price per share before the yield.
In B8 work out the price per share after the yield is added.
In B9 work out the shares minted for the deposit, rounded down with INT.
In B10 work out the value of those shares: shares times total assets after yield divided by total shares.
In B11 work out the rounding difference: deposit minus B10.

checks.label: B7 is the price before
B8 is the price after
B9 is the shares minted
checks.explain: Deposit times shares over assets, rounded down.

checks.label: B10 is the value of those shares
checks.explain: Shares times the price after yield.

checks.label: B11 is the rounding difference

activities.title: Build a token allocation table
activities.objective: Turn allocation percentages into token counts and test whether insiders hold too much.
activities.scenario: A project plans a supply of 1,000,000,000 tokens. Work out how many tokens each group receives and whether insiders hold a sensible share.
steps: In C2 work out the tokens for the first group: percentage times supply (B8) divided by 100. Fill down to C6.
In B9 add up the percentages to check they total 100.
In B10 add the percentages of the Team and Investors rows.
In B11 show Insiders hold too much if B10 is above 40, otherwise Balanced.

checks.label: C2 is the community tokens
C5 is the treasury tokens
B9 totals the percentages
checks.hint: =SUM(B2:B6)

checks.label: B10 is the insider share
B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B10>40,"Insiders hold too much","Balanced")

activities.title: Estimate the cost of an airdrop
activities.objective: Compare sending tokens to everyone with letting people claim, using gas figures.
activities.scenario: A project wants to give tokens to 20,000 people. Sending them directly costs gas for each transfer; a Merkle claim moves the cost to each claimant and costs one root upload. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In B7 work out the gas to send to everyone: recipients times gas per transfer.
In B8 work out the cost in ETH at the gas price (gwei): gas times gwei divided by 1,000,000,000.
In B9 work out the project's gas cost with a Merkle airdrop: just the root upload (B5).
In B10 work out the project's saving in ETH.
In B11 work out the cost in rupees of the direct airdrop at the ETH price (B6).

checks.label: B7 is the direct gas
B8 is the direct cost in ETH
checks.explain: Gas times gwei over a billion.

checks.label: B9 is the Merkle cost in ETH
B10 is the saving
B11 is the rupee cost

cells.A5: Gas to upload the Merkle root

activities.title: Final project: design a token for a real community
activities.objective: Produce a professional token design document covering purpose, standard, supply, vesting, controls, risks and launch.
activities.scenario: Choose a real community such as a coding club, a local business network or a school alumni group, and design a token for it. If a token is not the right tool, say so honestly.
steps: Add a Heading 1 with the project name and 'token design'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Purpose, Standard and parameters, Supply and distribution, Vesting, Controls and risks, Launch plan, Disclosures.
Under Supply and distribution list at least four allocation groups in bullets with percentages.
Under Controls and risks list at least four items in bullets.
State that the design is not legal advice and that legal and security review are needed before launch.
Mention one reason why a token might not be the right tool.
Keep it between 320 and 640 words.
